home.title: Is your pet’s food really as good as the pack says?
home.subtitle: Look up any dog or cat food and get an independent score from 0 to 100 – calculated from the ingredients and nutrients on the label, using veterinary nutrition guidelines.
home.searchHint: Tip: scan the barcode in the shop or type the EAN number.
home.step1Text: Search by name or brand, or scan the barcode with your phone. Dogs and cats are always assessed separately.
home.step2Text: Every food gets a 0–100 score with a plain-language breakdown: what is good, what is not, and how it compares with FEDIAF nutrition guidelines.
home.step3Text: Add your pet’s age, weight and allergies. Foods with ingredients your pet reacts to disappear, and you see the daily portion for your pet.
home.topText: Automatically ranked by score – no brand can pay for a place here. Scores describe the label, not a promise for every individual pet.
home.persTitle: A food guide that knows your pet

home.persA: Allergies and intolerances filtered out of every list
home.persB: Life stage, size and weight goals taken into account
home.persC: Daily calories and grams per day, calculated with FEDIAF formulas

home.brandText: Submit your products for free. We check every submission and score it with exactly the same method as every other food.

faq.a: No. The score rates what is printed on the pack against published nutrition guidelines. It cannot replace advice from your vet – especially if your pet has a health condition.

Out of 100 points: 35 for the nutrient profile (protein, fat, carbohydrates, fibre, minerals compared with FEDIAF), 50 for ingredient quality (where the protein comes from, how clearly it is declared) and 15 for a clean formulation (no sugar, colourants, synthetic preservatives). Everything is explained on the [methodology page](/{lang}/how-we-score).

faq.q: Do brands pay to get a better score?
faq.a: No. Scores are calculated by the same formula for every food. We earn a small commission when you order via our bol.com links, at no extra cost to you – see the [affiliate disclosure](/{lang}/affiliate).

faq.q: Why is a prescription or veterinary diet not scored?
faq.a: Therapeutic diets are designed for medical conditions and are meant to be used under veterinary supervision. Their nutrient profile deliberately differs from normal foods, so a general score would be misleading.

Not automatically. Grains are not harmful for most dogs and cats, and grain-free foods often replace them with peas or potato. We do not give points for grain-free – but you can filter for it, for example if your pet is allergic to wheat.

faq.q: How does the allergy filter work?
faq.a: Choose your pet’s allergens in the pet profile. Foods that list them are hidden. By default we also hide foods with vague wording such as “meat and animal derivatives”, because these can hide the ingredient your pet reacts to.

method.metaDescription: Exactly how the Scanabowl Score is calculated: nutrient profile, ingredient quality and clean formulation – with the scientific sources behind it.
method.title: How we score pet food
method.intro: Every food gets a score from 0 to 100. It is calculated by a fixed formula from the ingredient list and analytical constituents on the pack, using published veterinary nutrition guidelines. This page explains every step so you can judge it yourself.

pillar.nutrition: Do the numbers on the pack match what a dog or cat needs? Protein, fat, carbohydrates, fibre, minerals and – for cats – moisture, compared with FEDIAF.
pillar.ingredients: Where does the protein come from, how much of the recipe is animal-based, and is it declared clearly?
pillar.formulation: Points are taken off for added sugar, artificial colourants, synthetic preservatives and cheap filler.

sections.h: What the score is – and what it is not
p: The Scanabowl Score rates the **label**: the ingredient list and the analytical constituents printed on the pack. It cannot see how digestible a food really is, how well it is manufactured, or whether it has been proven in feeding trials.

The World Small Animal Veterinary Association (WSAVA) points out that an ingredient list alone says little about the quality of a food, and recommends also looking at the manufacturer’s quality control and research. Use our score to compare recipes and spot weak points – and talk to your vet, especially if your pet has a medical condition.

We convert the analysis to dry matter and to energy (kcal), so wet and dry foods can be compared fairly. If the label gives no energy value, we calculate it with the equation published by FEDIAF (based on NRC 2006). We then compare with the FEDIAF Nutritional Guidelines (2021):
ul: **Protein** – the FEDIAF minimum for adult dogs is 18–21 g per 100 g dry matter (45–52 g per 1,000 kcal), for adult cats 25–33 g (62.5–83 g per 1,000 kcal). Growing animals need more. Points rise above the minimum and then level off: more protein is not automatically better for a healthy dog.
**Fat** – FEDIAF minimum 5.5 g per 100 g dry matter for adult dogs (8.5 g for puppies) and 9 g for cats. Very high fat is penalised, as it promotes weight gain and can trigger pancreatitis.

**Carbohydrates (cats: 10 points, dogs: 4 points)** – estimated from what remains after protein, fat, fibre, ash and moisture. Cats are obligate carnivores: when they can choose, they select a diet with roughly 52% of energy from protein, 36% from fat and only 12% from carbohydrates (Hewson-Hughes et al., 2011). Dogs are more flexible, so carbohydrates count far less for them.

**Moisture (cats only, 7.5 points)** – cats have a weak thirst drive. Cats eating a high-moisture food take in more water in total and produce more dilute urine, with lower saturation of the minerals that form urinary crystals (Buckley et al., 2011).
**Fibre and ash** – too much of either lowers the score (a high mineral load matters especially for the urinary tract of cats).

**Dogs: calcium:phosphorus ratio and label completeness** – when calcium and phosphorus are printed, the ratio should lie between 1:1 and 2:1 (FEDIAF). Foods that print a complete analysis score better than foods that leave values out.

p: Ingredients are listed in descending order of weight *as mixed* – including the water in fresh meat, which makes up about 70% of its weight. So we estimate the share of each ingredient from its position and declared percentages, and compare on a dry-matter basis. That is why a food that starts with “fresh chicken” is not necessarily a meat-heavy food.
ul: **Protein origin (12 points)** – the estimated share of the food’s protein that comes from animal ingredients rather than plant concentrates such as gluten or pea protein. Cats need a higher share than dogs.
**Animal share of the dry matter (12 points)** – how much of the recipe itself is animal-derived.
**The first ingredients (10 points)** – is the list led by a named animal ingredient or by cereals?

**Named sources (10 points)** – “chicken” or “salmon” is precise. “Meat and animal derivatives” could be anything from muscle meat to feathers. By-products are not automatically bad, but you cannot see what you are feeding – and it makes allergies harder to manage.
**Useful extras (up to 6 points)** – EPA/DHA from fish or algae oil, prebiotic fibres, probiotics, glucosamine/chondroitin, taurine for cats.

p: We start at 15 points and deduct for things a pet does not need:
ul: **Added sugar** (sugar, caramel, syrup) – no nutritional need; cats cannot even taste sweetness.
**Artificial colourants** – they only make the food look better to the owner.
**Synthetic preservatives** (BHA, BHT, ethoxyquin, sorbates, nitrite) – natural alternatives such as tocopherols exist.

**Filler load** – for cats: a high share of cereals or plant protein concentrates; for dogs: a very high share of peas, legumes or potato. The US FDA has investigated an association between very legume-rich, grain-free diets and dilated cardiomyopathy in dogs. A cause has not been established – so this is a small deduction, not a ban.

p: If an ingredient is toxic for the species – for example onion, xylitol or chocolate, raisins for dogs, garlic or propylene glycol for cats – the score is capped at 25, whatever else is in the recipe.

sections.h: Dogs and cats are scored differently
p: Cats are obligate carnivores with specific needs (taurine, arachidonic acid, preformed vitamin A, a higher protein requirement), while dogs are more flexible. That is why the weights for carbohydrates, moisture and animal protein differ per species. We give no points for “grain-free” as such: grains are not harmful for most pets, and grain-free is not a quality mark. We do let you filter on it, for example for wheat allergies.

Veterinary and prescription diets, treats, supplements and complementary foods are not scored. Their purpose is different, so a general score would mislead. Foods without an ingredient list cannot be scored. When the analysis is missing, the nutrient part is a cautious estimate and we show a lower reliability.

The base score never changes. In your pet’s profile we add a personal match of at most a few points up or down for what the label cannot know: life stage (a growth food for an adult pet, or the other way round), a weight goal, dog size, urinary problems in cats and a sensitive stomach. Daily calories follow the FEDIAF energy tables (for example 110 kcal per kg^0.75 for an average adult dog, and 75 kcal per kg^0.67 for a neutered indoor cat).

In the pet profile you choose the ingredients your pet reacts to. We recognise each of them in Dutch, English, German and French label wording. Foods that name an allergen are always hidden. Vague wording such as “meat and animal derivatives”, “cereals” or “poultry” could contain it, so with the default setting those foods are hidden too. Fats and oils from that animal, such as chicken fat, count as well, because they can carry traces of protein.

The most common food allergens are, for dogs, beef, dairy, chicken and wheat, and for cats beef, fish and chicken (Mueller et al., 2016). A food allergy can only be diagnosed by an elimination diet with your vet.

Product data comes from public product information and from manufacturers who submit their products. We always check submissions before they are published, and the same formula is applied to every food – no brand can influence its score. We earn a commission on orders via our bol.com links; that is explained in the [affiliate disclosure](/{lang}/affiliate).
Spotted an error? Use the “Report a correction” link on the product page. We fix mistakes quickly.

about.metaDescription: Scanabowl makes pet food labels understandable with independent, science-based scores.
about.title: About Scanabowl
about.intro: Scanabowl helps pet owners understand what is really in their dog’s or cat’s bowl.

p: Pet food packaging is full of claims – “natural”, “premium”, “complete” – but the actual information is hidden in small print. Scanabowl translates the ingredient list and nutrient analysis into a clear score, with an explanation of every point.

ul: **Science-based** – our scoring follows published FEDIAF and NRC guidelines and peer-reviewed research, and we list our sources.
**Dogs and cats scored separately** – their nutritional needs are very different.
**Personal** – your pet’s allergies, age and weight change what you see.
**Independent** – brands cannot pay for a better score.

p: Scanabowl is free to use. When you order a food via our bol.com links, we may earn a small commission at no extra cost to you. That income is reinvested in the website. Read more in the [affiliate disclosure](/{lang}/affiliate).
Is your pet’s food missing? [Suggest it](/{lang}/suggest). Do you make pet food? [Add your products](/{lang}/brands). Found a mistake? Tell us via the [contact page](/{lang}/contact).

privacy.metaDescription: How Scanabowl handles your data: your pet’s profile stays on your device, and we only use your email address to reply to you.
privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: We collect as little data as possible. You can use Scanabowl without an account and without giving us any personal data.

p: The profile of your pet (name, age, weight, allergies) is stored only in your browser (local storage) on your own device. It is never sent to our servers, so we cannot see it. Clearing your browser data deletes it.

If you send a suggestion, correction, contact message or brand submission, we receive the information you enter (including your email address, if you give it). We use it only to review your submission and to reply to you. Product information you submit may be published on the site after we have checked it; personal details are not.

Photos you attach arrive as attachments in our e-mail. We use them to copy the product information. We only publish the photo of the front as a product photo if you give permission. Please photograph only the pack, not people.

We do not use advertising or tracking cookies. We store one small functional cookie (your chosen language, for one year) and local-storage entries for your pet profile. Because these are strictly functional, no cookie banner is needed. If we ever add analytics, we will use a privacy-friendly tool and update this page.

ul: **Vercel** hosts the website and processes technical data such as IP addresses in server logs.
**Resend** delivers the emails generated by our forms.
**bol.com** – when you click an affiliate link, bol.com and its partner platform may set their own cookies under their own privacy policy.

p: We keep messages only as long as needed to handle them, and no longer than two years unless the law requires otherwise.

Under the GDPR you may ask us for access to, correction or deletion of your personal data, and object to its use. Email us at the address below. You can also complain to the Dutch Data Protection Authority (Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens).

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: By using Scanabowl you agree to these terms.

p: Scanabowl provides general information about pet food. The scores and comments are not veterinary advice and are no substitute for a consultation with your vet. Always consult a vet before changing the diet of a pet with a medical condition.

We work hard to keep the data correct, but product recipes change and label information can be incomplete or contain errors. The score reflects the information we have. Always check the pack before you buy or feed. We do not guarantee that information is complete, current or free of errors.

Links to bol.com and other sites are provided for convenience. Prices, stock and delivery are determined by the shop. Any purchase is a contract between you and the shop; Scanabowl is not a party to it.

If you submit product information as a company, you confirm that you are authorised to do so and that it is accurate. You grant Scanabowl the right to publish and score this information. Submitting does not guarantee publication or a particular score.
The design, text, scoring method and software of Scanabowl are protected. You may share links and short quotes with attribution. Bulk copying of the database is not permitted without permission.

To the extent permitted by law, Scanabowl is not liable for damage resulting from the use of this site or reliance on its content. Dutch law applies, and disputes are handled by the competent Dutch court.

affiliate.metaDescription: How Scanabowl earns money through bol.com affiliate links – and why this never influences the scores.
affiliate.title: Affiliate disclosure
affiliate.intro: Scanabowl is free to use. This page explains how we earn money.

p: Scanabowl takes part in the bol.com Partner Programme. When you click a “View on bol.com” button and buy something, we may earn a commission from bol.com. It costs you nothing extra.

Scanabowl is an independent website. It is not owned by or affiliated with bol.com, and bol.com has no influence on our content, scores or recommendations. You place your order directly with bol.com, which is responsible for price, delivery and customer service.

ul: Every food is scored with the same formula, whether or not it is sold at bol.com or earns a commission.
Brands cannot pay for a place, a ranking or a better score.
The highest-scoring lists are generated automatically.

sections.h: How you can recognise affiliate links
p: Links to bol.com are marked as sponsored links and are accompanied by a short notice. Prices and availability are shown by bol.com; the price at the time you order is what counts.

sections.h: What we do with the income
p: The income is reinvested in Scanabowl: hosting, keeping the database up to date and building new features.
